Peters Bronx VAMC, 130 West Kingsbridge Road, Bronx, NY 10468 (“Bronx VA”) BACKGROUND: Through the HCHV CRS program, VA provides case management services to Veterans and facilitates their access to a broad range of medical, mental health, and rehabilitative services. Contractors must be able to provide care and sufficient services to Veterans who are homeless, in community-based residential settings. Each VAMC requires the contractor to offer a safe and secure environment to support Veterans’ rehabilitation and recovery goals. The contractor will be required to provide residential and case management services but will not be required to provide detoxification or other hospital level treatment. Those services will be provided by the VA at VA facilities or appropriate external service providers. The contractor will be expected to work collaboratively with a variety of VA programs and services to encourage Veterans admitted to the HCHV CRS Low Demand Safe Haven program to complete their agreed upon recovery goals. herapeutic and rehabilitative services determined to be needed by each Veteran admitted to the HCHV CRS Low Demand Safe Haven program. The therapeutic and rehabilitative services must be detailed in the individual service plan (a.k.a. “treatment plan”) developed by the contractor, with input from the Veteran (or designee) within 72 hours after admission. Services which the contractor must be able to furnish shall include: A variety of daily structured groups and activities provided by the contractor to promote social skills building and healthy lifestyle (i.e. resident participation in psychosocial group sessions, topics based upon resident preference and recommendations by the residential treatment setting staff and VA HCHV Liaison; physical activities; facilitated outings or social activities in the local community; social recreational/peer support groups, linkage to Alcoholics Anonymous, Narcotics Anonymous; linkage to vocational services/counseling). Daily activity schedules must be printed and posted in facility common areas to ensure Veteran awareness and promote participation. Health and personal hygiene maintenance; assistance to develop responsible living patterns, to maintain an acceptable level of personal hygiene and grooming, and to achieve a more adaptive level of psychosoci

ermined on an individual basis. CASE MANAGEMENT: Contractors shall provide, at minimum, the following case management services to Veterans in the program: Engagement of the Veteran in the service planning process. Contractor will carry the responsibility for interviewing, counseling and case managing for the identified Veterans by conducting psychosocial assessments to identify treatment needs which affect the Veterans’ adjustment to their environment and establish treatment goals. Contractor will utilize counseling strategies to include crisis intervention and case management including both short and long-term services. The VA has a strong preference for the use of harm reduction strategies in the case management process to effectively engage the population being served and maximize the chances for successful placement in community-based permanent housing as quickly as possible. Contractor shall assess the psychosocial and environmental needs or dysfunction secondary to or exacerbating the social, substance or psychiatric problems, which might contribute to the Veterans’ readjustment challenges in the community. Contractor establishes and maintains an intensive therapeutic relationship with the Veteran, family, staff, community programs/agencies, and is responsible for formulating case m

nd psychosocial services and documenting the overall effectiveness of the case management services provided. Specifically, but not limited to: Develop and complete a written Individual Service Plan (ISP) with the Veteran consistent with program goals within 72 hours of admission. Plan shall include provisions for Veteran placement in appropriate permanent housing within 60 to 90 days of admission to the HCHV Contract Residential Care facility but no more than 180 days without a planned reason for extension. Housing Placement planning must take into account all appropriate and available community-based housing options as well as the Veterans preferences regarding location and housing type. The plan should also be focused on getting the Veteran(s) to accept services, especially mental health and substance use services that will allow attainment of transitional or permanent housing. Acceptance of the services offered should not be a condition of continued stay in the contracted residential service program. However, engagement and service delivery should retain the expectation that the Veteran will advance to permanent housing with support, recognizing that it will often be at his or her own pace.
